utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis and Ekkehard Withopf, with Kimberly Fleming, the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And the appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, Stephane Bourgon, and Mirna Milanovic, our legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Mr. Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Mr. Nermin Mulalic, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber would like to greet everyone present, the Prosecution, the Defence, and the accused. We'll resume with the cross-examination of Witness XE today. But prior to giving the floor to the Defence to conduct their cross-examination, I would like to point out a few matters that concern clarifications. I'd like to point this out to the witness. Witness, you have taken the solemn declaration and you have sworn to tell the truth and nothing but the truth, which means that you should not lie and give false testimony. I would also like to point out to you, in accordance with Rule 90 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, that you can refuse to make any kind of statement that might incriminate you. And in such a case, the Trial Chamber has the right to force you to reply. If you answer the question, what you say in response can't be used as evidence against you. But this provision doesn't allow you to give false testimony, because proceedings can always be instituted against you for false testimony, whatever the case. So when a question is put to you, tell the truth and answer the questions put to you precisely. If you don't want to answer a question, tell us why you don't want to answer the question. The Trial Chamber is constantly monitoring your testimony, and naturally it is the right of the Defence to ask you any questions that they deem useful for the defence of their clients and to put any questions that are relevant with regard to the charges contained in the indictment. In addition, the Defence can also ask you questions that have to do with the general context within which the events unfolded. If you have any difficulty in answering a question, do inform us. So the Trial Chamber would like to ask you to answer the questions which are put to you, which is what you did yesterday when the Defence was conducting its cross-examination. The Defence may now proceed with their cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to ask whether protective measures were still in place. Is the procedure the same as yesterday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The protective measures are still in place. You have facial distortion and no one is aware of your name. If Defence counsel needs to ask you questions that might either directly or indirectly reveal your identity, that might have to do with your identity, in such cases the Defence will act in a professional manner, as it has done to date, and request that we go into private session before asking you such questions. So the Defence will bear your concerns in mind, and the Trial Chamber will do so as well. We are in open session at the moment. The proceedings will take place in open session, but protective measures are in place. And to fully inform you of everything, this means that when broadcast to the exterior, to the outside world, you will have facial distortion. You will benefit with facial distortion. And your name will not be mentioned. If there is something that might reveal your identity indirectly, we will redact this information. But we should point out that the proceedings are broadcast to the outside world but there is a 30-minute delay. So what is said at 2.25 will only be broadcast to the outside world after half an hour, so that gives us sufficient time to make corrections. At any point in time, the Defence can ask to go into private session. But if you yourself want to make such a request, if you want to request a private session, you should ask me. Have you understood what I am saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No audible response] MS. RESIDOVIC [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. And good day, Mr. XE.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Ms. Residovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to continue from where we stopped yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before that, while we're still in private session, I would like to ask the usher to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are not in private session. We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for my mistake, but it is not yet necessary to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we go into private session, I would like to ask the usher to distribute an additional translation of a statement into B/C/S to

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would also like to ask the witness to be shown his handwritten statement in B/C/S, in addition to this supplement, and also the statement that he gave to the OTP. I would also like to ask the statement of the Prosecution to be provided to the witness, which we will use in the course of our cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I would like to point out that the registrar should make an order to redact line 18, 19, and 20, as the police station in Boden has been mentioned and the date. And this could also enable the witness to be identified. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Has the usher also provided the witness with the B/C/S version which he identified yesterday, the B/C/S version of his handwritten statement and the B/C/S statement that he gave to the OTP? And could we now go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we'll go into private session. Mr. Registrar, please take the necessary steps.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session again. It's quarter past 5.00. We'll have a break, a half-an-hour break, and we'll resume at quarter to 6.00 and we will continue until 7.00. Unfortunately, the second witness might have to appear in the courtroom tomorrow, but we'll see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. I pointed out a moment ago that we will render our decision tomorrow morning regarding the admission into evidence of the documents produced by the Defence. Does the Prosecution also need to tell us their position? Perhaps they're not in a position to convey that position to us before tomorrow afternoon at the beginning of the hearing. If we hear that position of the Prosecution tomorrow, then we will render our decision later, in view of the fact that these documents have all been marked for identification only. We have one hour and 15 minutes, and we'll bring in the next witness. Mr. Usher, could you please bring in the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. Can you hear my words in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have been called to testify today by the Prosecution, and to do that you will first tell me your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bozo Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 2nd of August, 1957.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Miletici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not doing anything at the moment. I am sick. Yes, I am on sick leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And before being sick, did you have an occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I worked in Sumarija, the forestry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where are you living now? In what town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm now living in Srb, in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You will now read the solemn declaration in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may be seated. As you know, you have been called by the Prosecution to testify about facts that occurred many years ago. The Prosecution will have a series of questions for you. The Prosecution is on your right. And the Defence, who are seated to your left, will also have questions for you after the Prosecution. The Judges, who are in front of you, may also ask you questions if they consider that to be useful, in order to establish the truth. You have taken the solemn oath, so it is your duty to tell the whole truth and, therefore, to fully and with precision answer questions put to you. If you don't understand the meaning of a particular question, you can ask the person putting it to you to rephrase it. I wish also to inform you that if there are any questions which require answers from you which might incriminate you, at that point the Chamber may ask you to respond nevertheless, but what you say cannot be used against you. Similarly, as you are testifying after taking the solemn declaration, should you testify falsely, you could be subject to legal proceedings, to prosecution. Have you understood everything that I told you by way of introduction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand everything you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm now going to give the floor to a representative of the Prosecution, and I greet him, because he has just arrived. So, Mr. Stamp, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, can you briefly tell us the nature of your illness.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I have nervous trouble. I also have an ulcer and I have problems with my spine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From about when did you become afflicted with this nervous trouble?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Since 1993, when what happened happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the village and the municipality that you were born in.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Travnik municipality, the village of Miletici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you live in -- did you live there as well, up until 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you live there with your family?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you live in any particular part of Miletici?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which part was that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: At the end of the village, that is where my house was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there -- well, is there a part of Miletici known as Gornji Miletici and another one known as Donji Miletici?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. And I lived in Gornji Miletici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the ethnic composition of these two parts of Miletici at the time when you lived there.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: We lived well. No one offended anybody. Everything was okay, until 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Gornji Miletici was occupied by Croats or persons of Croat ethnicity in particular, and Donji Miletici was occupied by persons who were Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Croats lived in Gornji Miletici, and Muslims in Donji Miletici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what sort of work did you do until you left there in 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I worked in the Sumarija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: It is a company for cutting timber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the area where you lived, was there a school known as Zagradje?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is such a school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the -- in 1992, did you observe any particular type of activity that was being conducted there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is where the Mujahedin were staying, at the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if they -- well, can you describe what you mean when you say "the Mujahedin."

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: They were foreigners, foreign Muslim units that had come from Arab countries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they dress in any particular way or were they groomed in any particular way?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They wore white long shirts or something like dresses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from staying at the school, did these Mujahedin conduct any particular activities there, in relation to some members of the local Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Of course they did. The Muslims were with them in their units, and they were training the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were training which Muslims? Do you mean by that the local Muslims?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the local Muslims, the villagers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I'd like to take you to the 24th of April, 1993. That afternoon at about 5.00, where were you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I was tending my sheep. I had ten sheep, and I was grazing them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was this that you were grazing your sheep?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Just above my village, about 300 metres away from my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were doing this, did you see anyone approaching?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw they were coming in cars from Donji Miletici. I had no idea what it was all about nor who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after you saw these cars coming from Donji Miletici?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: They parked, and then three men came up to us, Dedo Suljic, Avdo Suljic, and Akif Suljic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These three men who came up to you, who were they? Did you know them before?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They are from Donji Miletici. I knew them from before. They were brothers, three brothers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: They were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These men that came up to you, did they tell you anything?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: They came to the village, and they said that we should all gather together in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else, if anything, did they tell you to do?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: They said that we should gather and that the Mujahedin had surrounded the village and that they would kill us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go on. Anything else they said?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They said, "We will protect you. You shouldn't flee anywhere."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you say or do anything?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I said at the time that we should flee. "How are you going to protect us when you have a son of yours in that unit?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Then we saw them approaching the village, and I fled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw who approaching the village?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I saw the Muslim army approaching.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can you tell us exactly what you saw.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I saw that they were coming towards the village with rifles and then they started shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just for the record, the village you're speaking of is Gornji Miletici?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Gornji Miletici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many households were there in Gornji Miletici at this time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I think about 13 households, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As these persons approached, they -- withdrawn. As the -- as the Muslim army approached, where were these persons, that is, the people who resided in Gornji Miletici?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: We had all gathered together at one spot, and then the children started crying and the women got afraid, and I said, "Let's run away," and we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many ran away?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No one. I did. The others stayed behind in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you run to?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I ran to my house, and then from my house I crossed over a wall and fled into the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you fled into the woods, did you see anything going on in the village?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: When I was fleeing, I didn't. But later, maybe an hour later, I saw them taking people out of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you see taking people out of the village?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I saw my parents being led out and all the other neighbours, who were tied up, including the children, and they were taking them away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So who was taking them away?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: The Muslims were taking them away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you when you saw this?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I was behind my house, about 300 metres away. I had some protection in the woods. And they were going along the road, so I could see them all as they were being led away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after you saw these people being led away? Did you remain in the woods, or did you go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I remained in the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I stayed there until darkness fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after that? Could you just relate to the Court in your own words what you did after that.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: After that, I spent the night there. I heard shots when they were taking these away. I spent the night there. And then in the morning, I went to the houses and I saw that some had been taken away, others were absent. I thought they were hiding someplace, so I went looking for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you heard shots.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- can you say, even approximately, where the sound of the firing of shots was coming from?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: This was happening in between the houses, so I couldn't really tell what the direction of the fire was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you went to the houses in the morning. About what time did you go to the houses?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what time it was, but it was early morning. It was light, and I went from one house to the next. I first went to my own house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what you saw and what you found as you went from house to house.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: When I went from my house, I went to Stipo Pavlovic's house. It was right next to my house. And when I went inside and opened the door, Stipo was lying dead in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what condition you saw his body in.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: His body was lying on its back, and on his forehead there was a hole above his eye. When I saw that, for the first time in my life to see a dead man killed in that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you saw Stipo, did you see anything else or anybody else in that house?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I passed by Stipo. The door was open. And through the door I saw Tihomir Pavlovic sitting on the sofa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he alive or dead?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No, he was dead. His hands were behind his back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what you saw. You said you saw him sitting. How was he sitting? Did you notice any injuries or anything like that? Tell us what you saw. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see any blood on him, but I did see some holes in his clothing. And I really was out of my mind. I couldn't take note of all the details then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anybody else in that house?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. On the floor, Franjo Pavlovic was lying. He was lying on his stomach. And there was a pot and his head was in the pot, and there was a soup ladle in the pot next to his head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the soup ladle, was there anything else in the pot?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No, just blood and the ladle, and he was lying on his stomach. I didn't see how this was done or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see anyone else apart from Stipo, Franjo, and Tihomir in that house?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Next to Franjo was Vlado Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe his physical condition as you saw him.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: He was lying on his -- on the side with his legs up. He knees were almost touching his head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else, if anything, did you notice about him? Did you notice any injuries?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't notice any injuries because I was so deeply shocked that I couldn't really look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he alive or dead?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Dead. Dead. He was dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to any other house after that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that Ante Petrovic was missing, and I went looking for him. And when I reached my uncle's house, I found him dead too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose house was it -- what's the name of the uncle?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: It was my uncle's house, in which Ante was lying dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's your uncle's name?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Ivo Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the condition of Ante Petrovic when you saw him that morning, the physical condition.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Ante Petrovic was lying. In his mouth, there was grass or something with thorns, and the television was right next to his head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the television exactly in relation to his head?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Right next to his head. Right next to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice if he had any injuries?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. All I could see was blood around him. I felt bad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if Tihomir and Vlado carried or bore arms, that is, weapons?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't carry arms. They were innocent witnesses. They hadn't joined any armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say they were innocent witnesses or something else?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: They were Jehovah's Witnesses, Jehovah's Witnesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic - and that is with your leave, Mr. President, if I may - Mr. Petrovic, we have some photographs of the bodies of these persons. Do you think you'd be in a condition to look at them and identify the persons?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the Prosecution is asking you whether, given your health, you'd be able to examine photographs that might bring back very unpleasant memories, shocking memories. If you don't want to have a look at these photographs, tell us. We will understand that your health is such that you don't want to have a look at them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If possible, I would rather not have a look at them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Prosecution won't show the photographs then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you saw the Muslim army approaching the village. Why do you say or why do you describe those who approached the village as the Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they were Muslims. That was their army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say how they were dressed, if you saw them with any uniform or any particular insignia?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, some of them were wearing white robes; others were in camouflage uniform. But given the state I was in, the stress I was under, and given that there was shooting, well, it wasn't possible for me to take everything in.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may just consult. One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The examination-in-chief has been concluded. Does the Defence have any questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, given the witness's condition and the facts that he has testified about, General Hadzihasanovic's Defence team doesn't have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have no questions for this witness either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, this concludes your examination. You have answered the questions put to you by the Prosecution. They have asked you a number of questions. And the Prosecution believes that it isn't necessary to ask you any other questions. The Defence hasn't deemed it necessary to ask you any questions, and the Trial Chamber doesn't think that it is necessary to ask you additional questions. We would like to thank you for having come to testify here in The Hague and for having contributed to determining the truth. The usher will now escort you out of the courtroom, and we wish you a good trip home. And we would like to point out that the Victims and Witnesses Unit will take care of you and organise your trip home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we have examined both witnesses, there is nothing remaining on our schedule. What is the situation for tomorrow, Mr. Withopf?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution will call the witness which is scheduled appearing for tomorrow on our confidential witness sheet. We anticipate the examination-in-chief lasting for one and a half, maybe up to two hours, so we should be easily in a position, including cross-examination and re-examination, to conclude and to finish this witness within the time frame given for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have one witness for Wednesday and we have another witness scheduled for Thursday, and on Friday two other witnesses will be appearing. I think that the schedule will be respected, and the witnesses that have been scheduled will appear. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Completely correct, Mr. President. We have one witness for tomorrow, we will have one witness for Thursday, who is likely to continue on Friday, and then we will have a second witness for Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Next week, as you know, Monday is a holiday. There won't be a hearing. We have one witness for Tuesday, the 3rd of February; another witness who is scheduled, for now, on Thursday, the 5th of February; and I think there will be witnesses -- on the 6th of February, there is no hearing. I think on the 4th of February -- do we have any witnesses for the 4th of February? Because according to the document that I have in front of me, dated the 22nd of January, there is a gap for the 4th of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, we today filed confidentially and we provided Defence with a copy of this information prior to the today's court session. We will have for sure five witnesses for next week, most likely even six witnesses for next week. We will have two witnesses on next Tuesday; we will have additional two ones for Wednesday; for sure we will have one for Friday and most likely a second for Thursday -- my apologies -- and certainly -- and most likely a second one for Thursday as well. The filing will detail which witnesses these are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the following weeks and months, the hearing will be continuous because we will have hearings until April without an interruption. As you know, there's the Friday before Easter which will be a holiday; Easter Monday is also a holiday. And if I have understood this correctly, according to the Defence they would like to have a few days -- a few additional days for various reasons, either to return to the territory of the former Yugoslavia to meet other people. And they have requested an interruption of the hearing because in January, February, March, and April the Trial Chamber will be sitting continuous. So I don't see that having a pause in April is a problem. But it would be best to have this break after Easter Monday, after the week that starts on Monday, the 12th and up to Friday, the 16th. So from Monday we will resume with the hearings. I wanted to point this out to the Prosecution so that the Prosecution could draft a schedule for his witnesses for the following week, for the week following the Easter break. This is the request made by the Defence. They want to have a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we would like to thank you, because that was the Defence's request and suggestion because having worked continually for three weeks -- for three months, it is the Defence's duty to examine how further investigations will be conducted, what the procedure will be in order to meet possible experts and to carry out other tasks that will facilitate the conduct of these proceedings without having interruptions. We would like to thank you. We request -- our request was made to have a break from the 5th and then stop after Easter or to start with the Easter holidays and then to have a break for a week, but we accept the suggestion you have made today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you. We accept your decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have no observations to make in that respect. We appreciate the reasons why Defence asked for such a short break. There's only one observation I wish to make for the record, and this is the following observation: We don't wish to count additional days against the time period that was given to us to present the Prosecution's case. Therefore, I would request the Trial Chamber to grant us additional four days at the very end of the current deadline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Given the way our work has been proceeding and given the witnesses that have been heard, is it Prosecution in the position to tell us, just as an indication, when it thinks they might finish -- conclude the presentation of their case? Will it be in mid-June, at the end of June? Is there an estimate, or are you not in a position to provide us with an estimate now?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, we are actually in a position to provide you with an estimate. Based on the decision of the Trial Chamber in the course of the Pre-Trial Conference that we have to present our case within a six-month time period, we always worked with the aim to comply with this requirement. And as it stands now, we are very, very likely to actually meet the deadline. As it stands now, we will have about 40 to 45 additional so-called crime-base witnesses with the current pace of about 6 to 8 such crime-base witnesses in a week. We anticipate finishing the crime-base evidence by end of March. We will then continue with so-called international witnesses. Of course, such international witnesses need a bit more time. We anticipate to complete their testimonies by some point in mid to end of May. We have a few former judges and prosecutors which will be called to testify for the Prosecution. The military expert will testify probably mid-May. We anticipate to have completed the presentation of the Prosecution's case by beginning of June. However, since the deadline has been given to us, I wish to use the opportunity to again respectfully request that the four additional days don't count towards the time frame given to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's not a problem. If you respect the schedule and in light of what you have just said, you should conclude the presentation of your case with the hearing of your witnesses by the end of May, beginning of June. So that should be possible, since, as you are well aware, at the end of this stage the Defence can make an application for an acquittal, and then there are deadlines that have to be respected, there are deadlines to respond to such a motion, deadlines for a decision to be rendered. So at the beginning of June would be an appropriate time, a perfect time, and that would give the Trial Chamber time to render any necessary decisions before August, since as you know there is a holiday in August and there will be a break in August. And hearings will only resume in September, at the beginning of September. But since we haven't had any -- since the schedule has been respected so far, we can inform the -- we take note of the fact that at the beginning of June the Prosecution will have concluded its case. With regard to the schedule, is there anything that the Defence would like to say?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Prosecution has presented its schedule for presenting its case to the Trial Chamber, and as we have already said, we will try to ensure that the Prosecution's evidence is presented within the specified time and we shall strive not to use up more time than the Prosecution when conducting our cross-examinations. We have no objections to raise, and we shall continue to strive to ensure that the proceedings are expeditious. With regard to examining the witnesses that the Prosecution has just mentioned - and this concerns the military expert and international witnesses - you are surely awaiting for a decision, as we are, which will enable the Defence to have access to the archives of the European monitors. According to the latest information -- my colleague, Stephane Bourgon, could provide the Trial Chamber with the latest information.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. On behalf of the two Defence team, I would like to inform the Trial Chamber about the most recent developments with regard to this matter. We have managed to contact the representatives of the European Union today, Mr. Mueller, who is responsible for the matter. He informed me that a draft response has been prepared for the attention of the Trial Chamber and signed by the secretary, Mr. Solana. This letter follows a series of consultations between the European Union and the member states of the European Union Monitoring Mission, according to the confidential procedure, which will be concluded today. So this draft letter could be forwarded to the Trial Chamber tomorrow with the response that was provided to us a little in advance. According to what has been drafted up today, the European Union will accept to give us access to the documents which were identified in the annex of our request of December and in accordance with the procedure suggested by the Chamber. All the documents will -- in a room in Sarajevo. We'll have access to this room in order to consult all the documents and to select the ones that we think are relevant. These documents will then be examined by representatives of the Monitoring Mission in order to determine whether they can be provided to us in their entirety or if it is necessary to redact parts of the document after the member states have commented on this. So this procedure could take place in the two upcoming weeks, and the Defence would then be in a position to have all the documents required for the presentation of the case. This should take place in two weeks' time. As you have suggested, Mr. President, and as you have understood on the basis of what my colleague has said, it won't be necessary to interrupt the proceedings in order to go and examine these documents. We will follow your suggestions and try and go and examine those documents without having an interruption in the proceedings. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for the good news that you have just informed us of, because we were not at all aware of how this matter was advancing. I'd like to turn to the other Defence team. With regard to the schedule, does the other Defence team have any comments to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have no objections to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So we have been able to take stock of the situation, given the time at our disposal. There are a few motions that are still pending, but the decisions will be rendered very rapidly and before the end of the week. That will enable us to advance with the proceedings. We will render a number of decisions which are being prepared. You'll be informed of them very rapidly. It's now 6.40. We will now adjourn, as we have no other witnesses, and we will resume tomorrow at 2.15, as scheduled. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 28th day of January, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.42 p.m.,
